text: Wnt7a signals through its receptor Fzd7 to activate the planar-cell-polarity pathway, driving symmetric expansion of satellite stem cells and enhancing skeletal muscle repair. In differentiated myofibres, Wnt7a binding to Fzd7 directly activates the Akt/mTOR growth pathway, inducing myofibre hypertrophy. The Fzd7 receptor complex was associated with Gα(s) and PI(3)K, and both components were required for Wnt7a to activate the Akt/mTOR growth pathway in myotubes. Notably, Wnt7a-Fzd7 activation of this pathway was completely independent of IGF-receptor activation. Together, these experiments demonstrate that Wnt7a-Fzd7 activates distinct pathways at different developmental stages during myogenic lineage progression, and identify a non-canonical anabolic signalling pathway for Wnt7a and its receptor Fzd7 in skeletal muscle.
